prompt.content:
You are analyzing the evaluation of one candidate change to a 3D-IC physical design flow.
Hypothesis of the change: The graph-cut partitioner's area-balance test uses a single global tolerance `area_balance_error` applied to `total_area`; tightening it from 10% to 5% forces the initial greedy and swap-based partitions to keep the two dies closer to equal area, reducing extreme die imbalance that causes long cross-tier detours and legalization displacement — a cheap, attributable probe of P-P4.
Rule-based digest:
total=-0.049 robust(mean-std)=-0.020 min_case=-0.019 all_valid=True
  ariane133-ng45: score=-0.011 dWNS=+6.8% dTNS=-6.6% overflow~156
  bp-ng45: score=-0.019 dWNS=-3.1% dTNS=-0.8% overflow~153
  bp_fe-ng45: score=-0.018 dWNS=+3.8% dTNS=-6.0% overflow~112
Write <=120 words. If some runs are INVALID (failures listed), first say what kind of failure it is (legality / crash / timeout) and whether it looks systematic (all seeds of a case) or sporadic - an invalid candidate says nothing about the hypothesis itself; suggest how to make the same idea legal. Otherwise: (1) did the hypothesis hold? (2) which case/metric moved and plausible mechanism, (3) one concrete next-step suggestion. No preamble.

response: The hypothesis did not hold: tightening area balance from 10% to 5% gave total −0.049 (robust −0.020), with all three cases slightly negative. Ariane133-ng45 improved WNS (+6.8%) but lost TNS (−6.6%); bp-ng45 and bp_fe-ng45 show mixed WNS/TNS with no clear imbalance-driven gain, suggesting the tighter tolerance added partitioning/legalization cost without reducing cross-tier detours. Next step: sweep tolerance (e.g., 10/7.5/5%) and log per-die area skew versus cross-tier wirelength and displacement to test the proposed mechanism directly rather than inferring it from WNS/TNS.
